question.text: Mutual Fund LTCG on equity-oriented fund (held > 12 months) post Jul 2024:

explanation.text: The Logic: Units of equity-oriented mutual funds held for more than 12 months qualify as long-term capital assets. Following the July 2024 Budget changes, their LTCG is taxed at 12.5% with the same Rs. 1.25 lakh annual exemption that applies to listed equity shares under Section 112A. The Trap: '10% above Rs. 1 lakh' was the pre-July-2024 rate-and-exemption combination; 15% applies to STCG on equity-oriented MF units, not LTCG; 20% is the post-July-2024 STCG rate on listed equity, again not the LTCG rate. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook supports the >12-month long-term classification for equity-oriented MF units (mutual-fund chapter pp. 110-123 and taxation pp. 185-190) but does not state the 12.5% rate or the Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption in the pages checked. The numerical framing above is based on the post-July-2024 Income Tax Act position rather than a workbook quote.
